review_notes: I read the whole file and the simp-tagged lemmas in it. The coe_/id/comp lemmas for mapHopfIdealPointsSubgroup and its Congr version are well oriented. The non-simp status of mapHopfIdealPointsSubgroupCongr_comp is documented and justified. I also read the FunctorOfPoints simp lemmas and the downstream uses of the membership lemma. The one concern is the @[simp] on mem_hopfIdealPointsSubgroup_iff. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about the simplifier's observed behaviour, only about which rules could apply.

findings.excerpt:
g ∈ hopfIdealPointsSubgroup n I A ↔
      ∀ x ∈ I, ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) n).symm g).ofConv x = 0
findings.problem: The general membership unfolding lemma is tagged @[simp]. It rewrites every membership in `hopfIdealPointsSubgroup` into a quantified statement about `(pointsMulEquiv n).symm g`. This competes with the file's own canonical reading for points. `pointToGeneralLinear_mem_hopfIdealPointsSubgroup_iff_toIdeal_le_ker` (not simp) turns `pointToGeneralLinear n (toConv chi) ∈ …` into `I.toIdeal ≤ RingHom.ker chi.toRingHom`. A simp call would apply the @[simp] rule first and give `∀ x ∈ I, ((pointsMulEquiv n).symm (pointToGeneralLinear n (toConv chi))).ofConv x = 0`. Neither side of this rewrite is a normal form in the other direction, and the result exposes `.symm` of an equivalence in the goal. Every downstream use rewrites it explicitly (`rw [...]` or `simp only [...]`), so the attribute is not used. The proof of the `_toIdeal_le_ker` lemma itself has to use `rw` followed by `simp only` to avoid depending on the attribute.
findings.proposed_change: Remove @[simp] from `mem_hopfIdealPointsSubgroup_iff`, keeping it as a plain `rw`/`simp only` lemma, which is how all callers use it. If a simp-normal form for points is wanted, tag `pointToGeneralLinear_mem_hopfIdealPointsSubgroup_iff_toIdeal_le_ker` @[simp] instead. Its LHS has the specific shape `pointToGeneralLinear n (toConv chi) ∈ hopfIdealPointsSubgroup n I A` and its RHS is a kernel containment. It is not blocked by the general rule once that rule is no longer simp.
findings.benefit: Goals about membership in a Hopf-ideal point subgroup are not unfolded by default into an expression with `pointsMulEquiv.symm`. The one canonical reading for an algebra-valued point, an ideal-kernel containment, is the only rule that can fire. Users of this subgroup, such as the UpperTriangular, Kostant and G2 files, keep control of the unfolding as they already do.
